claims.text: The target Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy initially has a non-equilibrium, metastable solid-solution-containing state.
The initial state has a homogeneous elemental distribution.
Thermal activation causes Mg atoms to diffuse out of the homogeneous solid solution.
Diffusing Mg becomes concentrated at grain boundaries.
Grain-boundary Mg enrichment facilitates nucleation and growth of Mg-rich intermetallic compounds.
Grain-boundary Mg enrichment facilitates formation of Mg-oxide precipitates.
Thermal exposure will produce fine Mg-rich intermetallic compounds and oxide phases at grain boundaries relative to the initial state.
The thermal evolution of Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloys is expected to involve intermetallic-compound formation.
Finely dispersed secondary phases can produce a continuous protective oxide layer or sheath.
Coarsening of the secondary phases can disrupt protective-layer uniformity and expose less-protective bulk phases.
Mg segregation and secondary-phase formation mediate changes in corrosion and high-temperature oxidation resistance.
Some thermal conditions will retain resistance through a protective oxide sheath, whereas others will degrade resistance by disrupting a uniform protective layer.
The transformations become significant above a threshold temperature and after sufficient time for Mg diffusion.
The proposed Mg diffusion behavior is analogous, although kinetically distinct, to Mn redistribution in a related high-entropy alloy.
High-temperature exposure can cause temperature-dependent oxide transformations and depletion of an oxide-forming element in a high-entropy alloy.
Treatments at 550 °C, 700 °C, and 900 °C represent relevant service-regime test points for the target alloy.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome allows retention of corrosion or oxidation resistance under some treatments, which could mean no statistically significant change from baseline, while the falsification rule declares absence of a statistically significant property change to be falsifying.
